summary.headline: Oriental Aromatics Q1 FY27 revenue rose 15% YoY to Rs 260 crore and EBITDA margin recovered to 7.62% sequentially, though still below 8.01% a year ago.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue from operations was about Rs 260 crore, up around 15% YoY but down 8% QoQ, with total sales volume up 22% and production up 18% YoY. EBITDA was Rs 19.8 crore (7.62% margin), up from 6.89% in Q4 FY26 but down from 8.01% in Q1 FY26 on higher raw material costs. PAT was Rs 2.51 crore versus Rs 3.98 crore in Q4 and Rs 0.5 crore a year ago. Mahad (Specialty Aroma Ingredients) remains under-utilised at 50-60% and is still weighing on profitability, with inventory building there. Management guided to 10-15% sales growth over the next year.

segments.name: Fragrance and Flavors (Ambarnath)
segments.commentary: Production and sales volumes marginally lower YoY, attributed to seasonality; management says the pipeline is healthy. Segment share of sales is roughly one-third.

segments.name: Specialty Aroma Ingredients (incl. Mahad)
segments.commentary: Healthy YoY growth in production and sales volume, but Asian capacity additions are pressuring selling prices. Mahad utilisation is 50-60%, with target of 75-80% for EBITDA breakeven; Mahad revenue is about Rs 3 crore per quarter per an analyst's calculation (not disputed by management).

segments.name: Camphor and Terpene Chemicals
segments.commentary: Strong YoY volume growth in the quarter, but domestic camphor faces structural overcapacity. Management said Indian camphor prices rose by a substantial double-digit percentage, driven by alpha-pinene up roughly 70-80% over five months.

guidance_outlook: Near-term goal of 10-15% sales growth over the next one year.
Mahad targeted to reach 75-80% utilisation, at which point management expects it to become EBITDA positive; no timeline given beyond 'next few quarters'.
Effective tax rate of about 25% for FY27 (management said same for FY28 was not specified).
Export share expected to stay in the same range (around 33-35%).
No margin guidance given; management said margin outlook is 'very fluid' given raw material and geopolitical uncertainty.
Priority is maximising utilisation of existing assets before major expansion capex.
capex_capacity: Mahad: 50-60% utilised; Phase-1 completed, with a large site for future molecules; commercialisation and customer qualification ongoing.
Most other plants (Specialty Aroma Ingredients, Camphor and Terpene, excluding hydrogenation) run at 85-90% utilisation.
Fragrance compounding facility has substantial headroom to increase production.
Management says no major expansion capex until existing assets are better utilised; capex cycle of the past 4-5 years considered largely complete by an analyst.
Specialty aroma commercialisation cycles take 500-1,000 days, per management.
demand_pricing: Specialty Aroma Ingredients: buyer's market with Asian (mainly China) capacity additions pressuring prices; pass-through achieved where possible, with step-up pass-through to cover FX and raw material costs.
Camphor: domestic overcapacity; management focusing on pharma-grade camphor, B2B relationships and Saraswati and 3 Pines brands. No progress reported on government discussions over camphor imports.
Part of Q1 volume growth was pulled forward by customers ahead of scheduled buying due to geopolitical concerns, per management.
Alpha-pinene (imported, USD-priced) up roughly 70-80% over five months and still firm; petro-based inputs volatile.
Premiumisation in personal care, home care and fine fragrances cited as intact long-term trend.
R&D spend around 2-2.5% of sales, per CFO.

qa_highlights.question: What is current utilisation for the overall business and Mahad, and what revenue potential exists at full utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Mahad is at 50-60% utilisation; most other plants at 85-90%. Management guided to 10-15% sales growth over the next year and did not give a long-term revenue number.

qa_highlights.question: How will margins and raw material costs evolve?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to forecast margins, calling the outlook 'fluid'. Alpha-pinene-based raw materials will stay expensive; petro-based inputs are seesawing.

qa_highlights.question: Volume growth of 22% versus revenue of 15%: what drove the realisation dip, and where do realisations go?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the gap to raw material-driven price increases and customers pulling forward allocated volumes. It declined to share division-level numbers.

qa_highlights.question: Tax rate for FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said about 25% for the full year, as parent and overseas entities carry no tax liability.

qa_highlights.question: Export contribution this quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: 35% in Q1 FY27 versus 33% in FY26; management expects it to remain in a similar range.

qa_highlights.question: Mahad revenue and whether production is being inventorised?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed inventory build-up at Mahad due to constrained access to a petro-based raw material; it expects to sell the inventory in the near future. No timeline given for meaningful scale-up.

qa_highlights.question: Saraswati and 3 Pines contribution, and camphor import pricing versus China?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to break out sub-division contribution and said it does not track Chinese camphor closely. Indian camphor prices rose by a substantial double-digit percentage.

risks_watch: Margin stuck around 7-8% for several quarters; Q1 EBITDA margin was 39 bps below last year, despite management's 'operational efficiency' messaging.
Mahad utilisation at 50-60% with inventory build-up; a meaningful scale-up timeline was not provided.
Asian capacity additions (especially China) keep pressure on Specialty Aroma and camphor pricing.
Alpha-pinene and petro-based raw material costs remain elevated and imported (USD-linked).
Q1 volume growth may have been partly pulled forward by customers, which could weigh on subsequent quarters.
Camphor import policy discussions with government have seen no further development.
Net profit very thin (PAT Rs 2.51 crore on Rs 260 crore revenue).
